food (47%), Red Meat (19%), and Rice (10%) constitute the largest
household food expenditure shares. Expenditure elasticity analysis
identifies Red Meat (=2.540), Poultry (=1.255), and Fish & Sea-
food (=1.349) as luxury goods, while staple items like rice and
sugar are necessities. Critically, rice commands the highest Marginal
Expenditure Share (0.293), indicating it is the primary recipient of
any additional household income. Own-price elasticities are nega-
tive for all commodities, with most being inelastic, confirming their
status as staples. However, demand for corn, soybeans, and red meat
is highly price-elastic. Cross-price elasticities reveal significant substi-
tution and complementary relationships among the food groups,
highlighting complex household consumption strategies. These find-
ings provide crucial, evidence-based parameters for policymakers in
East Java to design targeted food price stabilization policies and
social assistance programs that account for the heterogeneous con-
sumption behavior of households
